question_text: Juan is a 67-year-old natural-born Filipino citizen who has resided in the Philippines for the past 15 years. He was convicted of a crime involving moral turpitude 20 years ago but has since served his sentence and completed his probation. He wishes to vote in the upcoming national elections. Based on Article V of the 1987 Philippine Constitution, which of the following statements best describes Juan's eligibility to vote?

options.text: Juan is qualified to vote because he meets all the age, residency, and citizenship requirements, and his conviction does not permanently disqualify him.
Juan is disqualified to vote because his conviction for a crime involving moral turpitude is a permanent disqualification under the Constitution.
Juan is qualified to vote only if he applies for and is granted an absolute pardon from the President.
Juan is disqualified to vote because he is over 60 years old, which is the maximum voting age under the Constitution.
